tile_selection_basis: Both layouts were chosen from the fixed ROI and annotated bay spacing before running the detector. Three 600px tiles retain more neighboring-bay context (each tile is wider than one approximately 440px bay). Four 480px tiles reduce per-call scene width to roughly one bay while retaining 180px overlap for boundary context. This small comparison tests context versus saturation without using detector results to select a layout.
encoding: PNG from decoded source pixels; no resize
partial_edge_policy: Tiles are fully contained in the ROI. Origins are explicitly listed. The last tile is edge-aligned so the union covers the ROI exactly; if a future ROI is not exactly covered, use a full-size right-aligned edge tile and record its resulting overlap. Do not pad or resize.

three_wide.rationale: Three wide contexts, each slightly wider than one annotated bay; 35% overlap shares boundaries while keeping tile count low.

four_narrow.rationale: Four narrower contexts, approximately one bay wide; 37.5% overlap retains boundary context and tests whether reducing horizontal clutter avoids the cap.

deduplication.endpoint_proximity: At least one endpoint must be within the perpendicular tolerance of the other finite segment; this permits partial overlapping detections while rejecting nearby non-overlapping collinear segments.
deduplication.grouping: Deterministic complete-link grouping: a candidate must match every existing group member and a group may contain at most one detection from each tile. Reversed endpoint ordering is canonicalized.
deduplication.merged_geometry: For a duplicate group, take the union of projected intervals along a length-weighted mean orientation and use the median normal offset. This retains the observed union while not bridging gaps between non-overlapping fragments.
deduplication.provenance: Each deduplicated segment retains all original tile IDs, line IDs, origins, and mapped endpoints.
